title: Attorney General
lead: ==Article 76== provides for the Attorney General of India as the ==highest law officer of the Union== — a constitutional office, not a government servant, and a ==bridge institution across all three organs== of the State: advisor to the Executive, officer of the Court, participant in the Legislature.

items.title: Appointment & Tenure
bullets: By the ==President on the advice of the Government== (PM/Law Minister)
Must be ==qualified to be a Supreme Court judge==; citizen of India
Holds office ==during the pleasure of the President==; ==no fixed tenure==
Usually resigns when a new government takes office
Remuneration set by the Government — ==not charged on the CFI==

items.title: Advisory Functions
bullets: Advises the Government of India on legal matters
Gives opinions when referred by the President (==Art 143 references go to the SC, not the AG==)

items.title: Legal Representation
bullets: Represents the Union in the ==SC, High Courts and tribunals==
Handles major constitutional cases — Aadhaar, Sabarimala, Art 370 challenges

items.title: Legislative & Other Roles
bullets: May ==participate in Parliament proceedings== and give legal clarifications on the floor
Supervises the ==Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General==
Represents India in ==international legal matters==

items.title: Limitations
bullets: ==Not a government employee==; cannot be sued for advice rendered
==Cannot practise against the Government of India==
Cannot defend the accused in criminal cases without government consent
Cannot appear where the Government is an ==adverse party==
==Private practice permitted== → potential conflict between public duty and private clients

items.title: Importance
bullets: ==Guardian of constitutional values== — expected to uphold constitutional morality in advising the Executive
==Legal cohesion== — uniform litigation strategy across ministries
==Voice of the Union in court== — symbolically represents sovereignty
==Institutional memory== — continuity amid changing political leadership

items.title: Issues & Criticisms
bullets: ==Lack of independence== — office held ‘during pleasure’; criticised for defending government decisions over constitutional correctness (e.g. ==defence of the Aadhaar Act as a Money Bill, 2016==)
==No fixed tenure== — removable anytime
==Conflict of interest== from private clients
==No statutory duties or code of conduct== — unlike the UK's Ministerial Code
==Heavy litigation load== — the Government is the largest litigant
==Limited parliamentary accountability== — participates but does not vote or face rigorous oversight

items.title: Reforms Needed
bullets: ==Fixed tenure== — e.g. a 3-year term
==Statutory framework== defining duties, conflict-of-interest rules, ethical obligations
==Full-time position== — bar private practice, compensate accordingly
==Strengthen the law officers' cadre== — a professional legal service for government litigation
==Transparency in appointment== — a collegium-like consultative mechanism (PM, CJI, LoP)
==Parliamentary oversight== — regular reports to Standing Committees
==Reduce government litigation== via the National Litigation Policy
